ActionId.description: Identifies one dispatched Action inside a Run (RS-15).

local.description: Node-local ordinal, allocated by the owning registry.

Coercion.description: A value the Provider changed, with its reason (SB-44).

reason.description: The Provider's reason, uninterpreted by the Kernel.

ContentHash.description:
`sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`. The algorithm is named in the value so a later
algorithm is an additive change (OV-14).

Ident.description:
A name inside one document, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.

Names are compared as bytes; there is no case folding and no Unicode
normalisation, so the canonical form of OV-15 stays byte-comparable.

Rule: SB-1.

Key.description:
A `<vocabulary prefix><path>` or `ext.<module-id>.<path>` key.

The Kernel checks the prefix and the value's shape against the [`KeyDecl`] and
never interprets the meaning (audit Finding 7).

Rule: SB-2, MA-34.

Namespace.description:
A dotted sequence of [`Ident`]s owned by a Vocabulary or a Module,
matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$`.

Rule: SB-1.

NodeId.description:
A node in the (future) multi-host deployment. `LOCAL` is the only legal value in v4.0.

Rule: X7 (`00-overview.md`); it qualifies every id of TM-11, SC-6, SB-3 and MA-19.

Outcome.description: What `admit()` decided about one Session Action (RS-15, RS-16).

oneOf.description: It passed every check and was dispatched (RS-16).

coercions.description: What was coerced, including RS-19's "as soon as possible" (SB-44).

dispatched.description: The Kernel Actions it compiled to (RS-14).

oneOf.description: It was refused and never reached the real-time path (RS-16).

ResourceId.description:
Names a resource, or a sub-resource, inside the composite tree a Provider declares.

The path is a non-empty sequence of segments; `dev0/rx/0` names channel 0 of the
receive sub-tree of `dev0`. Vision §49 asks only for the node qualification; the
path replaces §49's flat `local` because a channel or a timekeeper must be
addressable (`00-overview.md` "Where these specs depart from the Vision").

Rule: SB-33, SB-34 (`03-spec-and-binding.md`), X7.

path.description: Slash-joined path through the composite resource tree (SB-34).

SessionAction.description:
The Session action envelope: a closed set, and **not** the Kernel Action set.

The Kernel's Actions are what a Reactor emits into the real-time path, while a
lease operation or a recorder request is a control-path act with no real-time
meaning. Each Session Action compiles to zero or more Kernel Actions, or to a
Lease or Run operation.

Only the lifecycle verbs are the Kernel's; a domain verb is
[`SessionAction::Vocabulary`], and the Vocabulary that registers the verb
declares how it compiles. Vision §3's log sketch names `StartRepeat` and
`Capture` directly; here they are `radio.start_repeat` and `sink.capture`,
because a Kernel that enumerated them would need a new variant for the first
peripheral sweep or calibration verb.

Rule: RS-13, RS-13a, decision R3.

oneOf.description: Generic over a namespaced key and value (RS-13a).
A domain verb, whose compilation its Vocabulary declares (RS-13a, RS-14).

at.description:
When. A Kernel field, not a param: SB-4 caps a `Value` at one level of
nesting and a `TimePoint` is two, so a time could not travel inside
`params` at all (RS-19).

ns.description: The Vocabulary that owns the verb.

oneOf.description: With a target it stops that resource; without one it stops the Run (RS-50).

target.description: The resource, or the Run when absent.

oneOf.description:
Reclaim a Detached Lease. Adoption by run id alone would let any client
seize a live transmitter (RS-24).

TimePoint.description:
An instant: integer ticks in a named clock domain. Never floating-point seconds.

There is deliberately no `PartialOrd`: two points of different domains cannot be
compared at all, and `a < b` silently answering `false` is the bug class this
model exists to prevent (decision T3).

Rule: TM-1, TM-6.

ticks.description: Tick count relative to the domain's origin; a sample index in a SampleClock (TM-10).

anyOf.description: A signed 64-bit integer, written as an exact decimal by the canonicaliser (OV-15).

A finite float; a non-finite one is refused rather than written as `null`,
because a `Value` reaches the sealed Manifest through `prepare.effective`,
the coercion records and the action log (OV-15, X9).
A list of scalars; nesting deeper is refused (SB-4).
A map of scalars; nesting deeper is refused (SB-4).

Value.description:
A scalar, or a list or map of scalars nested at most one level.

A Spec is data, not a document tree: one level is what a structured parameter
such as a capture request needs, and more invites the schema-inside-a-schema
that Vision §9 rejects.

Rule: SB-4.

key.description: Which key, when the violation names one.

Warning.description: A non-fatal note from a stage (SB-38, SB-41).

message.description: What it says; uninterpreted by the Kernel.

description: One entry of the action log (RS-15).

seq.description:
Dense: a rejected Action occupies one too, because a log with holes cannot
be replayed or audited (RS-15).

time.description: The Run-time instant at which it arrived (RS-15).

title: LogEntry
